feature: Ask makes a photo, vector art or a painting, from how you ask
summary: Ask now reads how you want a picture made. "A photo of a kitten walking in the snow" makes one real photograph as a picture layer, "vector art", "draw" or "an icon" makes editable vector layers as before, and "paint" makes one painted picture and says brushes are not ready yet.
setup: Photonz Dev, release Next, no flag changed from its default, with the picture model set up in Settings, Ask.

try.do: Open an empty picture, press Command K, type "a photo of a dog on a beach" and press Return.
Press Command K again and type "an illustration of a dog".
In a new picture ask for "make vector art of a fox".
In a new picture ask for "a painting of a harbour at dawn".
Ask for "create an icon of a camera".
Ask for "a dog on a beach", naming no kind: Ask picks, and the row says which.
Select a photo layer and add a shadow, round its corners or mask it, as with any picture.

evaluate: Do the photos look like photographs you would keep, at the picture's own shape?
Is about a minute for a photo an acceptable wait, with the row saying what is happening?
Does "No brushes yet, so I made one image." tell you clearly what you got when you asked to paint?
When you name no kind, does Ask's pick (a photo for a real place, animal or moment, a drawing for an icon or mascot) match what you meant?
Is typing "as a photo" or "as vector art" after a result the way you would want to flip it?
On the model sheet, is Z-Image's look good enough, or would you trade memory or time for Qwen's or MOSS's?
rough: Measured bar, Ask eval photo cases (contact sheet 2026-10-30-ask-photo-contact-sheet.png): before, the traced path scored 21.5, 21.5, 33.3 and 20.3 (mean 24.2), judged photographic 1, 1, 2, 1; now 93.6, 96, 76.1 and 95.2 (mean 90.2), photographic 9, 9, 7, 9.

Time and memory on this Mac (M4 Max, 64 GB): a photo is painted in 60 to 64 s at 1296 x 816 and the whole request takes 153 to 159 s; the picture model peaks at 13.3 GB. A traced drawing of the same requests: 35 to 52 s a painting, two or three paintings a request, 146 to 355 s in all, 13.4 to 14.0 GB at its peak.
The lighthouse "on a cliff" came out on low shore rocks (scored 76.1, did what was asked 6 of 10): the picture model's reading of the words, not routing.
A painting can carry a faint painted signature in a corner (the harbour, bottom right) although the prompt asks for none.
A photo is pixels, not paths: "make it vector art" makes a new drawing rather than converting the photo.
Painting with brushes stroke by stroke waits on the Brush tool task (a-brush-tool-paints-with-realistic-charcoal-chal); until then a paint request makes one painted image.
No mock covers making a photo with Ask; the one line Ask says above its rows sits where the Agent group already shows its rows.

Photo model comparison (sheet 2026-10-30-ask-photo-models-sheet.png, same four prompts, this Mac): Z-Image Turbo 55 to 74 s a photo at 13.4 GB, Qwen-Image-2.1 62 to 82 s at 30.6 GB, MOSS-Image 683 to 691 s at 21.2 GB. Z-Image stays: Qwen beside the 29 GB planning model would hold about 60 of 64 GB, MOSS is ten times slower. Qwen and MOSS did put the lighthouse on the cliff.
Held-out total: see the task log.
